title: Find out why Ask's held-out drawing and video scores fell between 7 and 8 November
goal: Ask's sealed test set scored lower on still drawings and video edits on 8 November than on 7 November, with nothing aimed at those changed on purpose. Find whether it is a real loss (and from which change) or run-to-run noise, so Ask is not quietly getting worse.
notes:
Seen, not explained. Scripts/ask-eval.sh time 20261108-075845-ask-held-out 20261107-130822-ask-held-out:
  8 Nov (41f4aabbe, 53 cases): total 56.9; drawing 63.1 (1 of 36 ran out of time, 4 stopped part way, 181s median), layout 68.1, redline 31.2, video 48.7, animated 37.3 (8 new cases).
  7 Nov (45 cases): total 66.4; drawing 70.8 (0 out of time, 2 stopped part way, 148s median), layout 44.6, redline 33.9, video 67.
Like for like on the 45 shared cases about 60.4 vs 66.4. Commit 41f4aabbe only changes the moving-icon route (AskMotion, MotionSVG folds, set_keys pivot for rotationX/Y), which drawing and video cases never take. Landed between the two runs: c41e1fcd3 (New window makes an animated icon), bf3e65120 (a round thing bursting opens), b491f6529 (torn icon teeth), the still icon route's breaks. Video is 3 cases, so one case moves the group ~18 points. Never read held-out cases one by one: rerun the whole set and compare totals and groups only.
acceptance: The held-out drawing and video group totals are measured again on current code and compared with runs 20261107-130822-ask-held-out and 20261108-075845-ask-held-out
The cause is named (a commit, the machine, or noise shown by a repeat run), in the task log with its numbers
If a commit caused it, a task to win it back is filed or the loss is fixed
